newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed sharply higher on Thursday after lower than expected U.S. May retail sales lifted markets on both sides of the Atlantic and Dutch players became reluctant to sell, traders said.
"The figures came in and all the bonds started to run a bit higher," one trader said.

U.S. retail sales fell for the third consecutive month. The 0.1 percent drop in May was also below economists' mean forecast of a 0.4 percent rise. The figures for March and April were also revised down to falls of 0.3 percent and 0.9 percent respectively.

After dull rangebound trading in the morning, the data at least encouraged some Dutch traders to become involved. A number noted more concerted buying of paper with maturities between 2004 and 2006. However, even with fresh afternoon energy, volumes remained low.
Some said there had been profit-taking of 10-year paper towards the close, but generally sellers had been scarce.
"There were hardly any sellers and that's why we've seen the big moves," one trader said.

Traders said today's gains were further discouragement for disinterested end investors. The yield on the benchmark ten-year bond, February 5.75 percent, fell by eight basis points to 5.58 percent. Traders said it would have to return to at least 5.70 percent for investors to appeal to investors.
"Six percent of course is the number many are looking for," one trader said.
